samples.summary: Read-only editor gate is bypassed by the pending-DOCX-import path that feeds `resetAfterDocumentReplace()`
samples.evidence: `initialize()` neutralizes every mutating EditorAPI method when `readOnly` is set (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3979-3997, allowlist `MUTATING_METHODS`), and this delta edits `resetAfterDocumentReplace` — which is NOT in that allowlist. Its only production caller (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:352-369) runs `store.setDocument(pending)` immediately before it, unconditionally, without consulting `readOnly` (the flag is available at line 327 where it is passed to `initialize`). A user holding only a viewer share link who has a staged import in `pending-imports.ts` for that document id therefore performs a whole-document overwrite through the client, side-stepping the read-only gate the rest of the surface enforces. `resetAfterDocumentReplace` itself does not mutate the Doc, so the finding is on the caller; server-side write authorization does exist (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 denies `rw` to non-editor share roles) but is disabled unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (line 86-88, shadow mode allows), so in a default deployment nothing else stops the write. Confidence is low because staging a pending import normally requires having just created the document, which a viewer would not have done.

finding.summary: Server-side write authorization for viewer share links is shadow-mode by default, so the client `readOnly` flag this change widens is the only effective write boundary
finding.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). Reported so the widened surface is weighed against the enforcement posture rather than assumed to be backstopped by the server.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 makes enforcement opt-in on the exact string 'true', and :97-105 discards the computed deny and returns ALLOW ('shadow') whenever enforcement is off; backend/README.md:111 documents false as the default. The only server-side write authorization for anonymous share visitors is hasAccess's `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true` at :200, which shadow mode nullifies. auth.controller.ts:76-84 mints a Yorkie token for any valid share token regardless of role and explicitly delegates role enforcement to that webhook, so a viewer-link holder can attach with verb 'rw' outside the browser app and write. The remaining boundary is the client-derived `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` at shared-document.tsx:152, and the change's own design doc (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:286-293) states this is the effective write boundary in shadow mode. No alternate server-side guard exists, so no already-guarded ground; the weakness is a weakened/unenforced authorization gate, squarely in the Security lane, and out-of-diff/pre-existing status does not exempt it under this rubric.
